contexts.text: The two things that constitute the whole man.
(Generals and particulars are) like a whole and its parts. A whole cannot be called a whole unless there are parts, since the whole consists of parts.
A total submission. Signified, Explained.

For the sake of making anyone blessed and happy, the Lord wills a total submission; that is, that he should not be partly his own, and partly the Lord's. (See ). A total submission is meant also in . And also in .

That the submission must be total, is evident also from the first (great) commandment (). Thus, as love to the Lord does not come from man, but from the Lord Himself, the whole heart, the whole soul, the whole mind, and all the forces, being recipients, must be the Lord's, consequently there must be a total submission.
For such as is anyone in the whole, such is he in the part; for they are... homogeneous.
A total falsification. Signified, Explained.
He is (then) clean every whit (). Explained.
What is wholly from good. Signified, Explained.
The head = the whole man, thus the whole. Explained, Illustrated.
There are two things which signify the whole, namely, the highest, and the lowest. Explained.
That the ultimate (or last) also = the whole. Illustrated.
That the feet, and the toes, and fingers also = all things, and thus the whole. Illustrated.
In every idea of thought which proceeds from the will there is the whole man. Explained.
That a man is wholly such as he is as to good, and not as to truth without good. Explained.
In the deeds, or works, is presented the whole man. Explained.
That the Lord wills to have the whole man whom He regenerates, and not a part. References.
When (things) become of a man's life, they become not only of his whole mind, but also of his whole body...
Through these principles (or beginnings) the life is, from every part, in the whole; and from the whole in every part. Explained.
In a word, the whole comes into existence from the parts; and the parts subsist from the whole.

Hence he who elevates his mind to the Lord, is elevated whole to the Lord; and he who casts down his mind to Hell, is cast down thither whole. And therefore the whole man comes into either Heaven or Hell, according to his life's love.
